## Convert to data frame with appropriately typed columns, and sort rows:
# colnames( poem_info ) <- c("title", "file", "n_word", "pub_date" )
poem_info <- data.frame( poem_info )
poem_info$file <- paste0( poem_info$file , ".html" )
poem_info$n_syl <- as.numeric( poem_info$n_syl )
poem_info$n_word <- as.numeric( poem_info$n_word )
poem_info$pub_date <- as.Date( poem_info$pub_date , format = "%d %b %Y" )
## Sort rows as desired:
# poem_info <- poem_info[ order(poem_info$n_word), ]
poem_info <- poem_info[ order(poem_info$n_syl), ]
# poem_info <- poem_info[ order(poem_info$pub_date), ]
## Result of above is a data frame with first row being placeholder and last row
## being placeholder, both of which have "file" as 'poems.html'.


## Function for creating next-poem links, as an html table that will be placed
## at bottom of each page:
next_link <- function( this_poem_file ){ 
  ## Assumes `poem_info` is global df, defined above:
  this_poem_idx <- which( poem_info$file == this_poem_file )
  table_html <- paste0(
    "<table style='width:100%'><tr>
    <td style='width:33%; text-align:left'>[&#8592; Previous Poem](" ,
    ifelse( this_poem_idx > 2 & this_poem_idx <= nrow(poem_info) - 1  ,
            poem_info$file[this_poem_idx-1] ,
            poem_info$file[nrow(poem_info)-1] ) # or "poems.html#sec-my_poems"
    ,")</td>
    <td style='width:34%; text-align:center'>[Poem List &#8593;](poems.html#sec-my_poems)</td>
    <td style='width:33%; text-align:right'>[Next Poem &#8594;](",
    ifelse( this_poem_idx >= 2 & this_poem_idx < nrow(poem_info) - 1  ,
            poem_info$file[this_poem_idx+1] ,
            poem_info$file[2] ) # or "poems.html#sec-my_poems"
    ,")</td>
    </tr></table>"
  )
  return( table_html )
}

# Function for a link that opens in new tabl:
link_new_tab <- function( url , display_text = url ){
  return( paste0( 
    '<a href="' , url , '" target="_blank">' , display_text , '</a>' ) )
}

# Function for creating html with qrc image, journal name, and pub info:
qrc_png <- function( qrc_url = "https://johnkruschke.com/poems.html" ,
                     journal_url = "https://johnkruschke.com/poems.html" , 
                     journal_name = "Journal Name" , 
                     publication_info = "Issue, Page, Date" , 
                     qrc_ht = 60,
                     pre_text = " First published in "
                     ){
  require("qrcode")
  # create filename, remove symbols from qrc_url:
  png_name <- qrc_url
  for ( split_at in c( "/" , ":" , "\\." , "-" , "_" , "=" , "\\&" , "\\?" ,
                       "%" , "#"  ) ) {
    png_name <- paste0( strsplit( png_name , split_at )[[1]] , collapse="" )
  }
  png_name <- paste0( "qrc_" , png_name , ".png" )
  # create qr code image and save:
  qrc <- qr_code( qrc_url )
  png( png_name )
  plot( qrc )
  invisible( dev.off() )
  # Return formatted image and text:
  img_str <- paste0( "<img src='" , png_name ,
                     "' height=" , qrc_ht , 
                     " class='image-left'>" )
  url_str <- paste0( "<a href='" , journal_url ,
                     "' target='_blank'>" ,
                     journal_name , "</a>" )
  end_str <- "<br clear='left'>"
  return( paste0( 
    "<div class='print-only'>",
      img_str , # <img ... >
      " John K. Kruschke<br>",
    "</div>",
    pre_text, 
    url_str , # <a href journal_name ... >
    ifelse( nchar(publication_info)>0 , ", " , "" ) , 
    publication_info , # volume, date
    " ",
    end_str ) )  # <br> etc.
}
